properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Type: Administrative

Violation Code: 78.12 - COMPLIANCE WITH PERMITS - Failure to comply with terms and conditions of permit or registration while drilling, altering or operating an oil or gas well.
Violation ID: 977102
Permit API: 083-57363
Unconventional: No
County: McKean
Municipality: Wetmore Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Partial Inspection
Inspection Date: 12/01/2022
Comments: Well drilled in to total depth. Production casing connected to production line with valve open. Temporary drill pit remains open onsite and is full of surface water. Well record review indicates that the well was drilled to a total depth of 2430'. A permit fee of $300.00 applies to a wellbore of 2001-2500' in length. The well permit application submitted by operator specifies an anticipated total depth of 2000'. A permit fee of $250.00 applies to a wellbore of 0-2000' in length. The total length of wellbore as drilled exceeds the permitted wellbore length by 429'. This act constitutes a violation of section 78.12 (Compliance with Permit) of 25 PA Code, Chapter 78 Oil and Gas Wells. Compliance with permit can be achieved as outlined in section 78.19(c) of Chapter 78, which provides: The operator shall pay the difference between the amount paid as part of the permit application, and the amount required under 78.19(a), Permit Fee Schedule. Operator was informed of the noted violation and remediation process via phone conversation on 12/01/2022 at 13:05.

Comments: On location to witness the conclusion of 72 hr. Stepped Pressure Build Up Tests (SPBUTs) being performed on all (5) wells on the Hunter pad., the Hunter 21HC, 22HC, 23HC, 5H and 6H. These SPBUTs are being performed to assess the recent remedial work, CET (Casing Expansion Tool), deployment performed on all (5) Hunter wells production casing strings. This is the 5th post CET deployment PBUTs being performed on these wells. - All (5) wells on the pad are in production. The (20x13) annuli are capped and set up to vent to atmosphere via Sentry valves. The (13x9) and the (9x5) annuli are set up to vent to a production tank via 2" common vent line. All annuli were closed when I arrived. - Upon arrival I met with CALLC Field Rep. Tyler Sites and Dalton Johnson and Creston Consultant Reps., Tom Messing and Andrew Pfisterer. Starting at approx. 10:45 ending annuli pressures were checked using a digital Crystal gauge. Gas checks were performed by Creston Reps., using a Bascom Turner Gas Explorer meter. properties.content:
Report Details

Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 8276973
Permit API: 015-23994
Unconventional: Yes
County: Bradford
Municipality: Pike Township
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 6/04/2026
Comments: On 06/03/2026 at 0017 hours the Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) received a notification of a release at Repsol's UGLIUZZA Well Pad in Pike Township, Bradford County (CTS #398207). Representative Ralph Babcock stated "on 6/2/26 at 5:15 p.m., a Keystone Clear Water truck driver was loading production water when the line split releasing 25 gallons of produced water. Approximately 10 gallons of produced water spilled into a containment structure while the remaining 15 gallons of produced water spilled onto the ground. Keystone Clearwater vacuumed produced water from the containment structure and scraped up impacted soil for later disposal.The DEP contacted Repsol and spoke with Mr. Babcock at 1145 hours. He stated the material from the release had been recovered and placed in drums onsite. He stated the release took place in the off-loading area of the pad. He stated he was notified of the released at 2345 hours (06/02).On 06/04/2026 the DEP conducted an incident inspection. I arrived at 0915 hours and met with Mr. Babcock. Environmental Resources was onsite to collect samples from the release and the prior release (CTS#396090). The area of the release was ~33 feet long (photo #2). There were no pooled fluids in the area of the release. Fluids on the pad surface were field measured for Electrical Conductivity (EC) between 452-1042 us/cm. The cause of the release was due to a valve malfunction (photo #3). Environmental resources screened the soil in the area of the release and received readings of 1-1.3 mS/cm (1000-1300 us/cm). The recovered material was observed in drums onsite and held within secondary containment (photo #4).The DEP screened the area of the prior release (CTS #396090). Fluids within the stormwater ditch at the release point were field measured for EC at ~452 us/cm. Mr. Babcock stated that this week there would be more material removed from the stormwater ditch at the release point due to elevated soil readings. There was dead vegetation observed downgrade of the affected bio-retention basin (photo #15-16). Fluids within and directly upgrade of the furthest downgrade sump pump were measured for EC between 1.248-2.24 mS/cm (1248-2240 us/cm) (photo #17 and 18). Fluids downgrade of the sump pump were field measured for EC between 173.7-398 us/cm. The violations related to the recent spill (CTS #398207) are considered immediately corrected however, outstanding violations remain open for API#015-23994 from the previous release (CTS #396090).I departed at 1120 hours.

County: Lycoming

Inspection Date: 4/18/2023
Comments: A follow-up inspection was conducted in order to assess conditions at the site after the reported release of produced fluid to the well pad on 3/3/23. The frac is still on-going on the pad. I met with company man Andrew Briggs upon arriving on location. Two puddles of fluid in the produced fluid off-loading area had an electrical conductivity (EC) of 2.44 and 3.61 mS/cm. The Department recommends vacuuming up this fluid. I told the company man my recommendation at the end of this inspection and he said that he would have the puddles vacuumed up. The puddles in the south travel lane had EC readings of less than 1000 uS/cm. The EC of the stormwater at the north corner of the pad was 795 uS/cm. The well site secondary containment appears to be in good condition. No holes or crushed berms were observed.Violations remain outstanding from the reported release of produced fluid to the pad surface on 3/3/23. Violations will remain outstanding until final approval is issued by the Department that Act 2 remediation standards have been attained.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 3/27/2026 to BIG DOG ENERGY LLC in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland county. 78a64a(a) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – Well site was not designed and constructed using secondary containment.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: BIG DOG ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 3/27/2026
Violation Code: 78a64a(a) - SECONDARY CONTAINMENT – Well site was not designed and constructed using secondary containment.
Violation ID: 8268926
Permit API: 129-25570
Unconventional: Yes
County: Westmoreland
Municipality: Hempfield Township
Inspection Type: Follow-up Inspection
Inspection Date: 3/27/2026
Comments: On 3/27/2026, the Department conducted an inspection at the Schimizzi S and M 1 well site in Hempfield Township, Westmoreland County. This inspection follows up to IR 4000998, where violations were left outstanding due to no observable Act 9 sign and available Emergency Response plan (ERP) onsite. Also, at the time of this inspection, no response of any kind has been received from the operator regarding violations issued in 3093059 or any subsequent cleanup that may have been conducted. At the time of IR 3484420, the soil conductivity onsite appeared to be comparable with that of the surrounding soil. At the time of IR 3978494, no staining or distressed vegetation was observed around the production tanks.The following was observed:No Act 9 sign is present at the well site entrance, and no ERP was found anywhere onsite (photo 1). The production tanks appear to be sound at the time of inspection, with no evidence of fluids leaking to the ground around them. However, they still lack compliant secondary containment to 78a.64(a), as is required at unconventional well sites (photos 4 and 6). No staining or distressed vegetation was observed on the ground around the gas well (photo 8). The well postings onsite include contact information for Dorso LP (photos 5 and 7). Outstanding violations issued against the operator's posted information are being overseen by the OG SubSurface team.The additional piping and production equipment that does not appear to be in use remains onsite (photos 10 and 11). Therefore, a violation shall be issued in IR 4170358 for failure to remove equipment that is not necessary for production, in accordance with in accordance with OGA3216(C).The well site overall exhibits greater than 70% uniform and adequate vegetative growth. No accelerated erosion and sedimentation concerns are observed at this time (photo 2).Based on observations from this inspection, violations that were continued in IR 4000998 shall remain outstanding, as it appears that no corrective action has been taken onsite since the date of that inspection and no response of any kind to IR 3093059 has been received to date.

Violation ID: 960903
Permit API: 081-20386
Unconventional: Yes
County: Lycoming
Municipality: Cummings Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/06/2022
Comments: On July 6, 2022, DEP representative Brad Kline conducted a site inspection at the Range Resources Ogontz 3H, 7-9H due to a reported spill of production fluid (CTS 365323). Range Resources Kirby Steck reported a spill of approximately 2 barrels of production fluid to the well pad surface and off the pad on July 6, 2022. A water tanker back latch was not completely sealed and when they were adding production fluid to the tank it started leaking and spilled onto the pad surface and over the pad slope to low spot off the southeast end of the pad. The area of impact off the pad was about 60 ft. by 10ft and about 6 inches in depth. On the well pad surface the impact was approximately 15 ft. by 15 ft and Range Resources had only scraped the top layer of stone to remove the impacted soil. The fill slope of the pad had a 4 foot wide area of impact from the top of the slope to the bottom of the slope which is approximately 10 ft. long. Later in the day on July 6, 2022, Mr. Steck left a message with DEP stating that after removing all the impacted soil that the volume of the spill of production fluid was closer to 3 barrels. The contaminated soil was being stored on separate containment from the plugging operations. Range Resources was waiting for covered dumpsters to arrive onsite. Moody is scheduled to be onsite on July 8, 2022 to collect confirmatory samples and begin the Act 2 process.The spill of production fluid outside of containment and onto the well pad surface and off the well pad is a violation of the Clean Streams Law 402(b), Chapter 78a.56(a), and the Solid Waste Management Act Section 301.

Comments: On April 24, 2025, an inspection was conducted in response to a spill at the Chabal 2 well site in Upper Burrell Township, Westmoreland County. According to the incident report that was submitted by the operator, this spill occurred on the day of this inspection at 12:45 PM and resulted in an estimated 50 barrel release of production fluids to the ground. This spill report was received by the Department at 2:16 PM.The Department spoke via phone with Penneco representative Marc Jacobs prior to this inspection, who explained that the brine tank valve failed and was ejected from the brine tank, which resulted in the release of an estimated 50 barrels of a brine and crude oil mixture. This was quantified based on the most recent fluid level measurement taken on the brine tank. No impacts to the Waters of the Commonwealth are reported to have occurred. Penneco representative John Dohman was present with the Department for this inspection. The following was observed:Upon arrival, the Department spoke with Mr. Dohman who confirmed that no impacts to the Waters of the Commonwealth have resulted from this incident. No identifiable water resources were visible from the location of the release. Mr. Dohman estimated that the release traveled approximately 70 yards down the slope adjacent to the brine tank and was stopped by a fallen tree. He explained that absorbent material was placed on the impacted area to absorb any standing production fluids and oil absorbent booms were placed downslope of the fallen tree that apparently stopped the release. Remediation of the impacted area is to be conducted by Moody and Associates and is scheduled to commence on the day following this inspection.The well head is equipped with a well tag appears to be free of fluid leaks at the time of inspection (see photos 2 and 3). The operator's information is posted on the separator (see photo 4). A gas odor was detected onsite during this inspection. An area of minor staining was observed on the surface of the well site (see photo 5). The body of the brine tank appears to be sound at the time of inspection (see photo 6). The failed brine tank valve appears to have been replaced (see photos 7 and 8). No fluids were observed escaping the brine tank at the time of inspection, therefore it appears that the release has been ceased. A path of brown staining was observed traveling downslope from the brine tank (see photos 9-18). The path of travel appears to be 70 yards, per Mr. Dohman's estimate. A faint crude oil odor was detectable from the impacted area. No evidence of visual impacts was observed downslope of the fallen tree that apparently stopped the travel of the released production fluids.Based on observations from this inspection, violations shall be issued from this inspection for releasing production fluids to the surface of the ground.The operator is requested to submit a written response within 15 business days of the spill or release. This response should include an incident report, a timeline, the regulation substance involved, where the spill or release occur, the environmental media affected, any impacts to water supplies, buildings, or utilities, and interim actions planned, initiated, or completed. The Department is requesting how the operator quantified the amount spilled. Any new impacts discovered or identified during interim remedial actions or site characterization should also be reported to the Department within 15 calendar days of discovery. Within 180 days of the spill or release the operator must perform a site characterization to determine the extent and magnitude of the contamination and submit the site characterization report to the undersigned. The operator shall assess impacts to waters of the Commonwealth from the spill or release.

properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: STONEHAVEN ENERGY MGT CO LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 5/11/2023
Violation Code: CSL 402(b) - POTENTIAL POLLUTION - Conducting an activity regulated by a permit issued pursuant to Section 402 of The Clean Streams Law to prevent the potential of pollution to waters of the Commonwealth without a permit or contrary to a permit issued under that authority by the Department.
Violation ID: 995089
Permit API: 053-29816
Unconventional: No
County: Forest
Municipality: Howe Twp
Inspection Type: Routine/Complete Inspection
Inspection Date: 5/11/2023
Comments: This conventional well is equipped with a pump jack that appears to have been recently produced. A sticker is posted on the pump jack displaying the operator's information, the well's API number is written on the jack. There was no activity onsite during this inspection. An approximate 2' x 5' area of vegetation and soil are stained with a coating of crude oil on the well site from the apparent repeated venting of this well into the atmosphere. The same practice is prevalent at a majority of the well sites on the Warrant 2980 lease and will be addressed in a separate inspection report. A tank battery that is located approximately 250' southeast of well consists of four steel and six plastic storage tanks inside of an earthen diking. There are several areas of stained gravel near the tanks (and at a compressor that is also located inside of the diking) which is indicative of production fluid releases onto the gravel inside of the containment.The exterior (southern) wall of the diking is void of vegetation and the specific conductance (SPC) is elevated (3800 uS/cm per field meter). It appears that the production fluid that has been released into the gravel inside of the tank battery diking has migrated through the southern wall of the containment and into a roadside ditch that flows south towards a cross culvert approximately 200 feet south of the well. Stressed vegetation, elevated SPC readings and abundant deer tracks are present in the ditch between the tank battery and the cross culvert and continue in a channel down to the next lease road (near 053-29533) approximately 300 feet beyond the culvert outlet.Multiple sections of the Warrant 2980 lease roads beyond this well to the vicinity of well #'s 053-29907, 053-29935 and 053-29916 have not been sufficiently maintained. BMPs (ditches and cross culverts) that are installed along these roads are not functioning properly, as a result, accelerated erosion is occurring over various stretches of the road surface. Additional E and S concerns on this lease are documented in the 5/11/23 inspection report for 053-29536 (Warrant 2980 #37).It is requested that documentation of production water disposal from this lease be provided to the Department. Please see the attached Notice of Violation regarding requested information pertaining to the cause of the release and intentions to remediate the contaminated material within and outside of the tank battery.

Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection conducted an INCIDENT inspection of the JKLM Sweden Valley 107 well pad located in Sweden Twp, Potter Co. on 6/3/2019 @1115 hours in response to notification of a spill, reported to the Department on 5/31/2019 @1535 hours. The weather was sunny, 54 degrees, winds WSW 5mph, gusts 10mph. Present onsite for the inspection were Terra Tokarz, Whipper Hill Consulting and Matt Skolny, JKLM. CTS report# 342615 states, JKLM reported a hose broke while pumping production water from the production water tank to the tank farm releasing approximately 3 to 4 barrels of production water; released water overwhelmed pump containment and spilled to gravel (soil/concrete) surface; JKLM utilized on-site vac truck to recover fluid. The following onsite conditions were observed during the inspection. The pump had been moved approximately 15' from the original spill location in order to allow for excavation of pad material impacted during the spill. Onsite personnel stated a valve, on a pump component, was left open while the operator traveled to another site to check on a different water transfer. This allowed the suction line from the pump to discharge production fluid, from the production tanks on the SV107, into it's secondary containment. The fluid over-topped the containment discharging an estimated 3 barrels of production fluid onto the pad surface. The fluid was recovered with a vacuum truck. Approximately 2-4" of pad material in a 35' x 70' area was excavated after a grid screening for conductivity, and placed in waste containers onsite. Penn E&R arrived onsite to collect confirmatory samples during the inspection. Violations of the following regulations are cited at this time: 25 Pa Code 78a.57 CSL 402(b) SWMA 301 I departed the site at 1245 hours.

Unconventional: Yes

Inspection Date: 12/22/2025
Comments: This inspection was conducted in response to a notification from the operator that a release of approximately 10 gallons of reclaimed stormwater occurred to the pad surface on December 20, 2025. A drilling rig remains in operation on the well pad. I met with Repsol representative Harry Lammy upon arriving on location. He accompanied me during this inspection and showed me the location of the release to the pad surface. According to Mr. Lammy, no fluid absorbed into the pad material since the ground was frozen at the time of the release. He also stated that the pad surface would be screened again for electrical conductivity following drilling operations to ensure that the pad material was not impacted by the release. The fluid released was stormwater which had been collected from the well site secondary containment, he also said. The impacted area of the pad surface was frozen during this inspection so that soil electrical conductivity readings could not be taken. Four GPUs have been installed on the well pad within secondary containment. Violations noted and are considered immediately corrected.

Comments: On 02/12/2026, a follow up inspection was conducted at the NV48 Well Site following violations issued on 01/13/2026. I was accompanied by Laura Grada (PA DEP).Violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), and 91.34(a) were issued on 01/13/2026 for the release of production fluid combined with freshwater. The quantity was approximately 5 barrels.The operator indicated that they were to remediate the spill following Act 2 guidelines; however the Department did not receive the Act 2 initial report within 15 days of the spill. This report is required by Chapter 78a.66 in accordance with Act 2.The following was observed:The impacted area was regraded, and the sumps appeared filled in (Photos 1, 2).The tanks which contained the spilled fluids were present on site; two tanks were in containment. Conductivity testing conducted adjacent to the containment yielded readings of 2.69 mS/cm and 6.82 mS/cm. I recommend additional remediation within this area (Photos 3-6).The largest section of the impacted area was relatively frozen and adequate conductivity readings were unable to be obtained. The area where the sumps were was frozen and displayed large amounts of ice (Photo 7). Additional readings will be taken once the ground thaws.The Act 9 sign was at the site entrance (Photo 8).The operator is in compliance with schedule regarding the violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), and 91.34(a). A new violation of 78a.66(c)2i is being issued for failure to submit the Act 2 15 day initial report.

Violation ID: 8153120

Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 7/18/2023
Comments: On 07/18/2023, an incident inspection was conducted at the Ironman Well Site in response to an incident report received by the Department and submitted by EQT on 07/17/2023 (CTS: 373620). I was accompanied by Matt Dracup, PGM (PADEP), Doug Oberdorf, and Jason Nicholson (EQT). Additional EQT and SPSI representatives on site. Stressed vegetation observed on north-northwest facing slope (fill side) of the Ironman pad on 07/14/2023 by an EQT contractor doing a routine site inspection. EQT representative investigated stressed vegetation on 07/17/2023 and identified it as a brine release and notified the Department. It was further investigated by EQT on 07/17/2023 w/ interim remediation activities starting on 07/18/2023. According to EQT, an approx. 5 ft x 2 ft pool of fluid was observed within area of stressed vegetation and fluid was observed sprinkling out. The overall area of stressed vegetation was approximately 25 ft x 25 ft. The release was estimated over a barrel and Act 2 remediation is anticipated. The source of the leak was identified as a small pinhole in cushion elbow at the northern most corner of the pad from the buried common dump line transferring brine flowback from the GPUs to the ASTs; approx. 70 ft northeast, away from the stressed vegetation area. Operator discovery and pre-remediation conductivity levels and incident writeup requested.Inspection observations: Area of stressed vegetation and pooled production fluid observed on fill slope below northwestern edge of pad and below compressor building on the pad. Among pooled fluid, an oily sheen was also observed. The impacted area appeared to be approx. 25 ft. x 25 ft. The area was covered with a plastic tarp upon arriving on site (Photos 1-7). SPSI crew preparing and beginning excavation to locate source of leak and begin remediation measures. Potholes to be dug on pad around approximate area of leak source to gain extent of fluid. Elevated conductivity observed within impacted area yielded readings of 14.62 mS, 9.96 mS. Readings beyond edge of impacted area, on the more northern edge of the area, displayed a reading of 1.87 mS. Additional readings within vegetation beyond edge of affected area were taken and yielded levels of 1.03 and within the area beyond the fence approximately 5 ft. at the bottom of the slope, 1.98 mS was observed within vegetation. Readings taken within the Unnamed Tributary to Daniels Run, below impacted area approximately 125 ft. north of the impacted area. Readings obtained within water and sediment of the stream w/ levels at 0.43-0.86 mS. Readings obtained within retentive berm along southeastern edge of site below pad; readings taken in water and within sediment yielded 0.33 mS and 0.60 mS (8-16). Readings taken at southern corner of the vegetated swales outlet structure, both in and around; readings of 0.46 mS within water and 0.59 mS within mud around the structure observed (17). SPSI began excavating a pothole, approx. 3 ft in depth; pooled fluid observed within. Conductivity reading within excavated hole was 6.30 mS. Vegetated berm adjacent to hole, above impacted area, displayed a reading of 0.34 mS (18-20). Additional readings within vegetation beyond western edge of impacted area displayed 2.21-6.44 mS (21-23). Reading in fluid contained within secondary containment around ASTs w/ level of 7.20 mS. Due to observed release of production fluid within vegetation on site and potential for fluid to impact WOC downslope of impacted area, violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued. Additional violations of 78a.66(b)(2) for failure to report within 2 hours, 78a.66(b)1(i), 78a.66(b)1(ii), and 91.33(a) for threatening WOC pollution, 5 gallons not completely contained and failure to report to DEP and downstream users are being issued. Additional follow up inspections to be conducted to monitor WOC downslope of impacted area.

Inspection Date: 7/18/2023
Comments: On 07/18/2023, an incident inspection was conducted at the Ironman Well Site in response to an incident report received by the Department and submitted by EQT on 07/17/2023 (CTS: 373620). I was accompanied by Matt Dracup, PGM (PADEP), Doug Oberdorf, and Jason Nicholson (EQT). Additional EQT and SPSI representatives on site. Stressed vegetation observed on north-northwest facing slope (fill side) of the Ironman pad on 07/14/2023 by an EQT contractor doing a routine site inspection. EQT representative investigated stressed vegetation on 07/17/2023 and identified it as a brine release and notified the Department. It was further investigated by EQT on 07/17/2023 w/ interim remediation activities starting on 07/18/2023. According to EQT, an approx. 5 ft x 2 ft pool of fluid was observed within area of stressed vegetation and fluid was observed sprinkling out. The overall area of stressed vegetation was approximately 25 ft x 25 ft. The release was estimated over a barrel and Act 2 remediation is anticipated. The source of the leak was identified as a small pinhole in cushion elbow at the northern most corner of the pad from the buried common dump line transferring brine flowback from the GPUs to the ASTs; approx. 70 ft northeast, away from the stressed vegetation area. Operator discovery and pre-remediation conductivity levels and incident writeup requested.Inspection observations: Area of stressed vegetation and pooled production fluid observed on fill slope below northwestern edge of pad and below compressor building on the pad. Among pooled fluid, an oily sheen was also observed. The impacted area appeared to be approx. 25 ft. x 25 ft. The area was covered with a plastic tarp upon arriving on site (Photos 1-7). SPSI crew preparing and beginning excavation to locate source of leak and begin remediation measures. Potholes to be dug on pad around approximate area of leak source to gain extent of fluid. Elevated conductivity observed within impacted area yielded readings of 14.62 mS, 9.96 mS. Readings beyond edge of impacted area, on the more northern edge of the area, displayed a reading of 1.87 mS. Additional readings within vegetation beyond edge of affected area were taken and yielded levels of 1.03 and within the area beyond the fence approximately 5 ft. at the bottom of the slope, 1.98 mS was observed within vegetation. Readings taken within the Unnamed Tributary to Daniels Run, below impacted area approximately 125 ft. north of the impacted area. Readings obtained within water and sediment of the stream w/ levels at 0.43-0.86 mS. Readings obtained within retentive berm along southeastern edge of site below pad; readings taken in water and within sediment yielded 0.33 mS and 0.60 mS (8-16). Readings taken at southern corner of the vegetated swales outlet structure, both in and around; readings of 0.46 mS within water and 0.59 mS within mud around the structure observed (17). SPSI began excavating a pothole, approx. 3 ft in depth; pooled fluid observed within. Conductivity reading within excavated hole was 6.30 mS. Vegetated berm adjacent to hole, above impacted area, displayed a reading of 0.34 mS (18-20). Additional readings within vegetation beyond western edge of impacted area displayed 2.21-6.44 mS (21-23). Reading in fluid contained within secondary containment around ASTs w/ level of 7.20 mS. Due to observed release of production fluid within vegetation on site and potential for fluid to impact WOC downslope of impacted area, violations of 78a.54, SWMA 301, 78a.57(a), and 91.34(a) are being issued. Additional violations of 78a.66(b)(2) for failure to report within 2 hours, 78a.66(b)1(i), 78a.66(b)1(ii), and 91.33(a) for threatening WOC pollution, 5 gallons not completely contained and failure to report to DEP and downstream users are being issued. Additional follow up inspections to be conducted to monitor WOC downslope of impacted area.

Comments: The DEP conducted an incident inspection of Repsol's Twin Ridge 02-185 well site located in Covington Township, Tioga County on 1/27/2020 at 1020 hours. The weather was 32 degrees with cloudy skies. This inspection was conducted in response to a reported release to containment on the pad. I spoke with Jeff Sparks (Repsol) onsite. On Saturday 1/25/2020, a hose connection between two frac tanks that were holding collected high pH stormwater from the basins onsite froze up and ruptured. The cold temperatures caused water to freeze and the expansion ruptured the hose connection between the two tanks pictured in photo #6. A reported two-foot level of water drained out of the tanks and into the secondary containment This resulted in an estimation of 100 barrels of released stormwater from the tanks. While onsite today, I observed a large volume of ice and water still present within the secondary containment. I told the operator that the containment should be cleaned out and inspected to ensure its functionality. Most of the fluids surrounding the containment and across the pad were frozen but any liquid water was screened for conductivity and pH. Puddles surrounding the containment were similar to those in other areas of the pad. No evidence was available to show that the secondary containment had leaked any volume of the reported release. The remainder of the site was routinely inspected. Crew were onsite today performing work on some of the processing facilities. All containment structures were intact and no leaks were noted. No erosional issues were found onsite today. Stormwater basins are continuing to be pumped out periodically. Violations cited on 6/24/2019 remain OUTSTANDING against API 117-21997 at this time. The violations will be closed once attainment with Act 2 standards has been confirmed. No additional violations were noted today.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 6/02/2022 to TURM OIL INC in Cherryhill Twp, Indiana county. 91.33(A) - INCIDENTS CAUSING OR THREATENING POLLUTION - Failure to notify the Department of an accident or other activity or incident, a toxic substance or another substance which would endanger downstream users of the waters, result in pollution or create a danger of pollution of the waters of this Commonwealth, or would damage property.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: TURM OIL INC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety

Violation Code: 91.33(A) - INCIDENTS CAUSING OR THREATENING POLLUTION - Failure to notify the Department of an accident or other activity or incident, a toxic substance or another substance which would endanger downstream users of the waters, result in pollution or create a danger of pollution of the waters of this Commonwealth, or would damage property.
Violation ID: 957715
Permit API: 063-34032
Unconventional: No
County: Indiana
Municipality: Cherryhill Twp
Inspection Type: Complaint Inspection
Inspection Date: 6/02/2022
Comments: On 6/2/22 at 0900 hrs., I conducted an inspection of Turm Oil, Inc.'s Paul Strong 4 well (API 063-34032) in Cherryhill Twp., Indiana Co. Mr. Bill Davis with Turm Oil was also present during the inspection. The inspection was conducted in response to a complaint, received by the Department on 6/1/22, of oil and produced water being released from a production fluids tank that was being removed from the site.I spoke with the complainant, the operator, and Mr. Davis on 6/1/22. The operator informed me that the well was sold to Rosebud Mining back in March; however there is no record of a well transfer filed with the Department. During our phone call, Mr. Davis informed me that the tank removal and release occurred around 1100 hrs. on 5/31/22. He estimated that approximately 10 gallons of crude oil and production fluid was released when removing the tank, and stated that some absorbent material was placed near the well and was subsequently containerized. Mr. Davis also acknowledged that some released fluid was covered up during regrading of the site.Upon inspection of the site, oil stained soil and vegetation was observed, beginning at the regraded area of the well pad, and continuing along a drainage ditch adjacent to the pad. There was a strong crude oil odor present. The impacted water in the ditch flowed to a nearby ephemeral stream where a slight sheen was observed. The black plastic bag containing the absorbent material Mr. Davis previously applied was located at the base of the well head; however, no additional measures were taken to prevent the material from reaching Waters of the Commonwealth. I advised Mr. Davis to place absorbent boom or pads to prevent further downstream impacts. I also advised Mr. Davis that regulations require removal of the pollutant from the soil and water within 15 days. In addition, I requested that Mr. Davis reinstall a well tag with the permit number on the well head.The release was not reported to the Department. Violations of 91.33(A), 78.66(a), 91.34(A), 78.66(b), and78.66(e) are cited and will be immediately closed as 'unresolvable'.Violations of CSL 301, CSL 307(a), CSL 402(b), 78.54, 78.57(a), SWMA 301, SWMA 302(a), and SWMA 610(1) are being cited for the release of crude oil and production fluid onto the ground and into Waters of the Commonwealth. These violations will be resolved upon remediation and temporary stabilization of the site, and submission of waste manifests for the disposal of impacted material to the Department.

properties.summary: Environmental Health & Safety violation issued on 11/30/2022 to JKLM ENERGY LLC in Ulysses Twp, Potter county. 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
properties.content:
Report Details
Inspection Client: JKLM ENERGY LLC
Violation Type: Environmental Health & Safety
Violation Date: 11/30/2022
Violation Code: 78a56(a) - TEMPORARY STORAGE - Operator failed to contain regulated substances and wastes used at or generated at a well site in a tank, series of tanks or other storage structures approved by the Department.
Violation ID: 977492
Permit API: 105-21923
Unconventional: Yes
County: Potter
Municipality: Ulysses Twp
Inspection Type: Incident- Response to Accident or Event
Inspection Date: 11/30/2022
Comments: The Department of Environmental Protection (DEP) conducted an INCIDENT inspection of the JKLM - Headwaters 146 Well Pad located in Ulysses Twp, Tioga Co on 11/30/22 @1300 hours in response to a release of between 5 and 42 gallons of completions fluid into secondary containment and onto the pad surface. The weather was 45 degrees, rain, winds W @15mph. Terra Tokarz, JKLM Env Field Coordinator was present onsite. JKLM was in the process of dewatering a transfer line into the frack tanks when a cam lock on the hose failed. Mrs. Tokarz stated the majority of the fluid was captured by the tank secondary containment, but a revised estimate of 10 gallons was released to the pad surface in a spray. The impacted area was approximately 15' x 30" off the back side of the frack tanks. Approximately 1" of pad material was removed from the impacted area and placed in a dump truck on secondary containment until a waste container could be procured. The area was screened for field conductivity and found to be <1.0mS/cm. Elevated fluid was still located in the secondary containment. Mrs. Tokarz stated the vacuum truck onsite is routinely removing the fluid from the secondary containment. JKLM stated they had screened the pad E and S controls and no elevated conductivity was found. Due to conditions onsite observed during this inspection, it appears the spill has been adequately remediated.Violations of the following regulations are cited as IMMEDIATELY CORRECTED against the 2HU (API#105-21923) well:25 Pa Code 78a.56(a)SWMA 301CSL 402(b)I departed the site at 1430
